newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels say 84 fighters killed in attack.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels say 84 fighters killed in attack.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger guerrillas on Saturday said 84 of their fighters were killed in an attack on a military camp in the island's east, contradicting the government's death toll.

The Defence Ministry said at least 200 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels were killed and more than 120 wounded during Thursday's pre-dawn attack on Vaunathivu camp in Batticaloa, about 200 km (125 miles) from Colombo.
The LTTE's clandestine Voice of Tigers radio quoted the rebels' official newspaper "Eelanatham" as saying 84 rebels were killed, including two high-ranking guerrilla officers.
The radio, monitored in the government-controlled northern town of Vavuniya, did not give the number of rebel wounded.
The Defence Ministry said on Friday that 65 soldiers, including two officers, were killed and 35 were wounded when some 800 LTTE fighters attacked the camp.
Rebel suicide bombers launched a simultaneous attack on China Bay air force base in Trincomalee, 240 km (150 miles) northeast of Colombo, killing an airman and destroying a transport plane.
The rebel newspaper carried a photograph of three "Black Tiger" suicide bombers with the LTTE's leader Velupillai Prabhakaran, taken shortly before they left for the China Bay attack, the radio said.
"The LTTE, which deliberately kept a low profile for the past several months, proved once again they can launch fierce attacks in any part of the north and the east," the radio said.

The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, offered little resistance to a military offensive last month that captured a key highway linking two army-held northern towns.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the number is much higher.
